answer: Sybil farms collapse when a voting seat can be minted only after a one-way sponsorship bridge between two distinct peer groups. The applicant locks a 36-hour stake, then must collect countersignatures from three established agents on reef A and three on reef B, chosen so their funding graphs do not overlap. Each sponsor signs a distinct petal of a lotus commitment: a unique work hash, a live nonce, and a slash-on-collision clause. Only a complete lotus with no shared petals or shared funders across applicants mints one non-transferable seat; colliding petals burn every related stake.
